bounds.domain: One existing campaign with allocation5, initial spent2, two delete callers and at most two attempts each. Money is integral in this instance; a corrupt retained numeric input is an explicit unavailable state. The parent organization and source ownership remain present.
bounds.atomicity: One primary SQL transaction locks the organization, deletes and returns the current campaign, refunds its unused allocation and inserts both linked financial receipts. Credit, advertising or suppressed-row failure rolls back every mutation; cache invalidation occurs only afterward.
bounds.scope: Real PGlite service/repository tests check SQL failure and suppressed receipts, linked ledgers, post-commit cache failure, zero refund, corrupt numeric rejection and foreign-organization refusal. SQL lock scheduling, provider truth, external deletion/creation races, debit/budget-update protocols, decimal rounding and general TypeScript refinement are not proved here.
bounds.providerBoundary: This is the SQL settlement phase after no external campaign exists or its provider deletion was confirmed. Unknown external deletion, stale provider spend, and retries against an already-deleted remote resource remain separate unresolved lifecycle obligations; there is no remote exactly-once claim.
bounds.progress: Weakly fair SQL and reply continuations settle accepted calls. Failure may preserve the campaign for retry. No provider availability, elapsed deadline, successful deletion or automatic replay guarantee.
bounds.conformance: Four independent-session PostgreSQL cases observe lock blocking for competing deletes, spend-before-delete, delete-before-spend and rollback-to-waiting-writer. These are selected real SQL histories, not a complete isolation proof.

assumptions: Weak fairness of the finite SQL/reply continuations. External provider creation/deletion happens outside this modeled phase.
